A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FTCT study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison; the existing appendices can be matched despite renumbering.

before.justification: v6 reports original Transformer and MLP experiments, attention analyses, linear probing, and appendix robustness evaluations, including Figure 2 and Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v8 retains these original empirical results, including the main experiments and appendix evaluations of noisy inputs, larger models, and incomplete reasoning paths.

M1.justification: The FTCT procedure, underlying program, Transformer construction, and inference procedures are unchanged. Algorithm 1 retains the same in-context learning and parent-retrieval steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic FTCT coverage, including complete chains, noisy testing sequences, varying chain lengths, and incomplete intermediate reasoning paths. The new related-work discussion introduces no evaluated dataset or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same five Transformer configurations and two MLP configurations. Newly cited methods such as Back Attention appear only in related work and are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The graph-depth and child-chain settings, prompting procedures, accuracy metrics, model configurations, auxiliary training data for larger models, and probing protocols are unchanged across corresponding experiments.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same architecture comparisons, noisy-input tests, training-coverage checks, chain-length sensitivity analysis, attention/probing analyses, and missing-step evaluations. The supplementary analyses in v6 Appendices H–M match v8 Appendices I–N.

E5.justification: v6 Appendix H.1 and v8 Appendix I.1 both report means and standard deviations over five causal-structure variations per graph-depth/child-chain setting. The uncertainty displays and reported repetition information are unchanged.

E6.justification: The reported results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 2–13 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains whole-chain accuracies of 0.996 for the 3-layer/3-head Transformer and 1.000 for the 2-layer/2-head Transformer under the same settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Lemmas 5.1–5.3, Theorem 5.4, and constructive proofs are retained. v6 Appendices D–F correspond to v8 Appendices E–G; their differences concern references, typesetting, and text flow.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about few-shot CoT, training-testing similarity, model complexity, and an underlying program implemented through induction heads and attention assignment.

C2.justification: The study's mechanism explanations and qualifications are unchanged, including excess-shot degradation, possible larger-model overfitting, limited transfer to natural-language models, and failures with missing intermediate steps. Appendix A situates the existing CoT finding within cited research without revising these interpretations.

D1.justification: The code link, data-generation instructions, tokenization, and Transformer, MLP, and probing specifications are retained. Implementation details move from Appendix G to H, preserving settings such as 720-dimensional embeddings, a 2048-token context window, and AdamW with learning rate 5e-5.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands positioning through twelve works on compositional generalization and implicit versus explicit multi-hop reasoning, covering grokking, reversal effects, optimization, and coverage limits. Section 2 also substitutes Shi et al. (2024) for Wei et al. (2023), and the Allen-Zhu and Li Part 3.2 reference is removed. Other venue/year updates largely concern retained works.

P1.justification: v8 inserts the related-work appendix, renumbers the existing appendices from A–M to B–N, and updates cross-references and bibliographic wording. The main section sequence and nearly all existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–13 and Tables 1–4 retain their designs and contents. Limited text reflow changes spacing and the placement of Algorithm 1 relative to the FTCT examples and proof; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Appendix A fills a gap in v6's discussion of closely related research, connecting FTCT's explicit prompting result to recent compositional and latent multi-hop reasoning studies. This improves scholarly context while preserving the original evidence and limitations. The overall gain is limited because the experiments, theory, and reproducibility information are unchanged.
